title: Children on a Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) Surviving Spouse Award
content:
Adjudication guidance on adding and removing children on a Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) award held by a surviving spouse.

## Adding a child

A child is added on a dependency report received online or by mail. The addition is effective on the birth or adoption date when the report arrives within the dependency report window of that date. A telephone report cannot add a child.

## Removing a child

A telephone report can remove a child. A child is removed:

- the day before the child's birthday at the child age limit; or
- the last day of the month in which the child marries or dies.

A child permanently incapable of self-support before 18 stays on the award without an age limit.

Each child addition is removed only once.

## Children paid outside the spouse's award

A school child from 18 to the school-child age limit receives DIC in their own right, not on the spouse's award.

## How a report is received — what it can do

| Channel of the dependency report | Can add a child | Can remove a child |
|---|---|---|
| Online | Yes | — |
| By mail | Yes | — |
| Telephone | No | Yes |

## Event — removal date

| Event | Child removed on |
|---|---|
| Child reaches the child age limit | The day before that birthday |
| Child marries | The last day of the month of the marriage |
| Child dies | The last day of the month of the death |
| Child became permanently incapable of self-support before 18 | Not removed by age; stays without an age limit |

## Removal once per addition

Each recorded child addition can be ended by one removal only. Where VA's records already show a removal against that addition, it is not removed a second time; the record of that addition, not the caller's recollection, shows whether it has been removed.

## Hypothetical cases

- A child born on February 11 is reported by mail within the dependency report window of that date. The child is added effective February 11.
- A child on the award marries on September 6. The child is removed on September 30.
- A child dies on May 2. The child is removed on May 31.
- A child who became permanently incapable of self-support at age 12 reaches the child age limit. The child stays on the award.
- A school child who has turned 18 receives DIC in the child's own right, not on the spouse's award.
